answer: The jade multiplier is published, charged in thread, and ridge lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3943 identities would post 2866 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
